# Review disclaimer and savings-note copy

## Review disclaimer — include verbatim as a comment above every wrap

```
This wrap was generated by Claude and hasn't been run — review it before dropping it
into your codebase. It's a reasonable starting point, not a guarantee: the error signal
fed to LoopGain, the target_error default, and (for framework-specific loops like
LangGraph/CrewAI/AutoGen) whether the right adapter was used are all judgment calls a
one-shot rewrite can get wrong.
```

As a Python comment block:

## Savings-note guidance — literal/structural agent loops only

Pair the user's own literal fact with the published aggregate benchmark — never invent a
per-repo number. The published figures: **92.8% cost reduction, ~15× faster wall-clock,
2,000 paired real-API trials, vs. a fixed `max_iterations=20` baseline, quality preserved
or improved.**

The reasoning must genuinely differ by `current_stop_mechanism` — three distinct notes,
not one template with nouns swapped:

- **Fixed iteration count** (`detected_cap` is a real number): "This loop pays for the
  full `N` iterations on every run, regardless of when it actually converges."
- **No explicit bound**: "There's no fixed cap here, so the worst case is genuinely
  unbounded — nothing today caps how much a stuck loop could cost."
- **Custom convergence check** (the code already has some kind of stop condition): "This
  loop already has some convergence awareness. What LoopGain adds on top: divergence
  detection (stopping early if things are getting worse, not just checking a threshold)
  and best-so-far rollback (returning the best output seen, not just the last one)."

## No savings claim for semantic-loop candidates

The published benchmark above was measured on agent loops with hard, measurable error
signals. Do not extend it to semantic/reasoning-loop candidates (Step 3's fourth
category) — there is no equivalent published number for that case, and inventing one
would violate the same "never fabricate a per-repo/per-case number" rule this whole
skill is built around. For those candidates, the wrap's comment should describe what
LoopGain adds (divergence detection, best-so-far rollback) without a percentage or
multiplier.
